problem: Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(0.94)^{5}.$ Give your answer to three decimal places.
worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{5} & =1+5x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{5} \\  & =1+5x+10{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{5}≈1+5x+10{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.06$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{5}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0.94)^{6} & =(1+(-0.06))^{5} \\  & ≈1+5(-0.06)+10(-0.06)^{2} \\  & =1-5(0.06)+10(0.003\,6) \\  & =1-0.3+0.036 \\  & =0.736,\end{aligned}
$$

to three decimal places.
